item.title: Is Iran Shaping Up to Be a ‘Forever War’?

item.title: Teachers Want Screen Time Limits In School, Too
item.description: A new Gallup poll found that a majority of teachers “strongly” or “somewhat” support screen time limits in school, but the policies are hard to enforce.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mervosh
item.media:credit: Gabriela Bhaskar for The New York Times
item.media:description: In elementary school, students spend over a quarter of their class time on devices for allowed activities.

item.title: Scrutiny of Jury May Complicate Future of Lindsay Clancy Case

item.media:description: Kevin Reddington, Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer, could try to argue that the lone holdout juror who caused the hung jury would never have been seated if a past criminal accusation against him had been known.

item.title: Court Tosses Immigrant’s Conviction Over Agents’ Secret Facebook Group

item.title: A.I. Is Unpopular With Voters, a New York Times/Siena Poll Finds
item.description: As fears grow about the threat of artificial intelligence, neither party has claimed an advantage on the technology, a New York Times/Siena poll found. But voters are united in opposition to data centers.

item.media:description: A data center under construction last year in Abilene, Texas. The enormous computing complexes have become unpopular with voters and a significant issue in the midterms.

item.title: Supreme Court Stands Up to Trump on Mail Voting and a Few Key Issues

item.dc:creator: Adam Liptak

item.media:description: The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s latest attempt to change mail-in voting rules on Monday.

item.title: Trump, the Supreme Court and the Postal Service: A History of Mail Voting
item.description: The mail system took on new prominence during the Civil War by enabling soldiers to vote from afar. On Monday, the Supreme Court blocked President Trump’s effort to give it a new role in elections.
item.dc:creator: Dan Watson
item.media:description: Two U.S. service members talked over their absentee ballots outside a bunker in Korea in 1952.

item.title: Congress Has Proposed Many Bills for A.I. Regulation. Lawmakers Have Enacted Few.
item.description: For years, Democrats and Republicans have proposed bills to address the greatest threats posed by artificial intelligence. Many remain stymied by political disputes.

item.media:description: Democrats and Republicans in Congress have issued a battery of measures focused on A.I., but lawmakers have largely failed to enact any of the proposals.
